Why the FOCUS Framework Matters in Real-World FinOps


When you’ve worked with cloud bills for long enough, a few truths become obvious.
Every cloud provider structures data differently


Normalizing cost and usage data across teams is a pain


Building dashboards is easy — making them reliable and actionable is not



That’s where the FOCUS Framework steps in.
FOCUS stands for FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification. It's a standard schema for representing cloud cost and usage data — regardless of provider.
Think of it as a common language for cloud billing data, whether you’re using AWS, Azure, GCP, or all three. It’s open, extensible, and vendor-neutral — built by practitioners through the FinOps Foundation.

articles.author: TheAngmarCore
articles.description:
Telegram has long ceased to be an anonymous space. Knowing just your ID (@username) or phone number, someone can learn almost everything about you.
From the groups you belong to, what you wrote there in the past (including some deleted messages that may still exist in archives), whom you talked to, which voice notes or media you posted — even private chats you're a part of (if they were once public), your previous usernames, and potentially even personal data, geolocation, and more.
The main source of such information? Telegram bots.
How to become a "ghost" on Telegram?
• Don’t use unknown Telegram bots.
• Don’t use your primary phone number.
• Hide your name.
• Avoid using @usernames.
• Don’t share personal information.
• Configure your privacy settings.
Remember:
Absolute anonymity on the internet is impossible.
You always leave digital footprints that can be traced back to you.
But minimizing them — is absolutely possible.
articles.title: Guide to Data Protection on Telegram
